 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Holalkere, by judgment and award dated 28.06.2018 passed in MVC No.562/2016.
2. The factum of accident, injuries sustained and coverage of insurance, are not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.
4.

The medical records on record proves that the claimant has suffered following injuries:
(i) 1 x 1 cm and 0.5 x 0.5 cm abrasions (ii) LE-Open Globe Injury and other injuries in grievous in nature 5.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:2575 Sl. Amount Particulars No. in Rs.
1

Towards pain and suffering 25,000/- 2 Towards loss of amenities and 10,000/-
happiness and frustration of life 3 Towards conveyance, attendant, 5,000/- food,
nourishment charges 4 Towards medical expenses 10,463/-
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is lesser and the Tribunal has not followed correct parameters while determining the compensation.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation.
7. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained and treatment undergone by the claimant, a compensation of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under the head 'pain and suffering' in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal, which would result in a sum of Rs.65,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,463/- towards medical expenses based on the medical bills produced by the claimant.

But considering the medical reports and medical bills produced by the claimant and the fact that claimant has undergone eye surgery of his left eye at Shankara Hospital, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head Sri K Chandrappa vs Ramesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145413769/
3
'medical expenses', in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal, which would result in Rs.60,463/- and rounded off to Rs.60,000/-.

9. Taking into consideration that claimant has undergone surgery of left eye and the period of hospitalization, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards 'loss of amenities and happiness and frustration in life'.

Looking into the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities' in NC:
2024:KHC:2575 addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal, which would result in Rs.30,000/-.
11. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards 'food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges', which is on lower side.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head 'food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges' in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal, which would result in Rs.20,000/-.

12. Thus, in all claimant is entitled to compensation as follows:
Sl. Awarded by Awarded by  Particulars No. the Tribunal this Court  1 Pain and suffering 25,000/- 65,000/-

2 Medical expenses 10,463/- 60,000/-
 3 Loss of income during  laid up period -- 15,000/-
 4 Loss of amenities 10,000/- 30,000/-
 5 Food, nourishment,
 conveyance and  attendant charges 5,000/- 20,000/-
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.50,463/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,90,000/-.
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,39,537 (Rs.1,90,000/- - Rs.50,463/-).

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,39,537/-, which is rounded off to Rs.1,39,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Sri K Chandrappa vs Ramesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145413769/
4 14.

Respondent No.3 is the insurer of Maruthi Omni car and the accident is between the Maruthi Car bearing registration No.KA-05/MH-9740 and Maruthi Omni Car bearing registration No.KA-14/N-7515 and both the drivers have contributed negligence towards the accident.
As per the records it is proved that the accident has occurred in the middle of the road and therefore both the drivers have contributed to the accident.
Hence, both the insurers and vehicles are indemnified to pay the NC: 2024:KHC:2575 compensation 50% each.
Therefore, respondent Nos.2 and 3 being the insurers of the vehicles are directed to pay 50% of compensation each to the claimant.

15. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.
 ii. The impugned judgment and award  dated 28.06.2018 passed in MVC No.562/2016 by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Holalkere, is modified to the extent that the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,39,500/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. No order as to costs.
iv. Draw award accordingly.
